note: Every combination of the axes below is run. Distinct schedules are counted by the runner from the actual traces; the number is recorded, not assumed.
Expected values come from the baseline criteria (1)-(7) and from the hand-derived rule tables below. They are not generated by the model.

Timeline conventions (annex/E3-RECOVERY.md section 5, P-E3-1): generation R boots at r; fence issued r, confirmed r+1; reload clicks r+3; read r+4; checkpoint issued r+6, confirmed r+7; B from T2 at r+10 (settles r+11), C from T1 at r+13 (settles r+14), both on the final generation W.
Under the singleItem control the initial store is the single item holding {k0:'a'} (that alternative has no versioned records).

first.P0: gen1 dies at t=10, before A reaches it (no set)
first.P1: A = ['k1','x'] issued at 10 as (1,2); gen1 dies at 20 with A pending
first.P2: A issued at 10, applied at 15 (no settle); gen1 dies at 20
first.P3: A issued at 10; storeTimeout reply at 5010; gen1 dies at 5020 with A pending
first.fail: A issued at 10, its promise REJECTED at 15 (reply transport); T1 sends A' = ['k1','q'] at 16, issued (1,3), settles ok at 17 (reply null); gen1 dies at 20. A is later applied at its L (the baseline 'fail' variant; this violates A15d on purpose)

second.P4: gen2 boots, its fence write never settles, it dies at r2+9 (during the epoch write). R = gen3
second.P5: gen2 confirms, reads at r2+4, issues checkpoint (2,0) at r2+6 and dies at r2+7 before it settles. R = gen3

extraDeath.yes: R dies at rR+9 after its snapshots and before any data write; W = R+1 writes B and C

positions.L2: after R's fence confirmation, before R reads the key (rR+2)
positions.L3: between R's read and R's checkpoint (rR+5)
positions.L5: after B, placed after C has also settled (rW+15); P-E3-2: the latest 'after B' moment, the one where the baseline says singleItem fails

axes.spacing: each new generation boots 50 ms after the previous death

criteria.c1: k0 = 'a' in every snapshot and in the final dictionary
criteria.c2: final dictionary contains k1 = 'z' and k2 = 'y'
criteria.c3: every snapshot of generations >= 2 taken before C settles has the same k1 value (or all lack k1), equal to rule k1First
criteria.c4: no reply to a message of a dead generation, no duplicate reply, every reply from the accepting generation while alive
criteria.c5: epochs of the generations that wrote records are strictly increasing in boot order, and no record name is issued twice
criteria.c6: no snapshot before that generation's checkpoint is confirmed
criteria.c7a: the greatest record ever present is never removed, and no record is removed unless a greater record of the key is present
criteria.c7b: FakeBackend metric only (names count, len(name)+len(compact JSON value)) stays <= STORE_RECORDS_MAX / STORE_DISK_HARD. This is NOT the D104 bound: fmt 2 sizes, DiskLedger and reserves are rows E4/E6

k1First.when: first in {P1, P3} and L(A) in {L1, L2} and not (second = P5 and L(CP2) in {L1, L2})

rules.derivation: R reads the largest valid record present at rR+4. Candidates: gen1's (1,1); A as (1,2) if applied before the read (P2 at 15, or L1/L2); gen2's checkpoint (2,0) holding {k0:'a'} (gen2 read before any L1 apply; for P2 it also holds k1:'x') if applied before the read. A (1,2) < (2,0), so CP2 shadows A. R's checkpoint (E_R, 0) is larger than every gen-1 and gen-2 record, so later applies never surface (lemma: browser.md:597-600).
